newsitem.title: UK: BOXING-"CELTIC WARRIOR" COLLINS RETAINS WBO CROWN AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-"CELTIC WARRIOR" COLLINS RETAINS WBO CROWN AGAIN.

text.p: Steve "Celtic Warrior" Collins retained his World Boxing Organisation super-middleweight crown for the sixth time on Saturday, stopping Frenchman Frederic Sellier in the fifth round.

The referee ordered a halt in front of a sell-out crowd at the London Arena after Ireland's Collins drove a heavy right hand through the Frenchman's defences to open up a deep gash on the bridge of his nose.
"He was a durable guy, but he cut up pretty bad," Collins said. A glancing blow in the second round had left the Frenchman with a cut on his left eyebrow.
After the fight, Collins took the opportunity to lay down the gauntlet to International Boxing Federation champion Roy Jones of the U.S.
"Roy Jones, I'll fight you anyhow, anytime, any place," he said.

On the same bill, Britain's Robin "Grim Reaper" Reid knocked out South African Giovanni "No Mercy" Pretorius with a scything right hook in the seventh round to retain his World Boxing Council super-middleweight belt for the first time.

Pretorius barely survived the first round after a deluge of blows left him sitting on the canvas. He picked himself up to mount a brave counter-attack, but after another knock-down in the fifth, Reid delivered the decisive blow two rounds later.
